body.cap: Marketon’s newly unveiled ‘Mobile Hologram’ device features high-quality 3D visuals projected in mid-air, controllable without direct touch | Photo by Marketon

body.x: Immersive display technology company Marketon (CEO Chang Joon Yang) has officially unveiled its next-generation ‘Mobile Hologram’ product, designed specifically for K-pop fans. The device merges AI agent technology with holographic display capabilities, enabling users to project high-quality 3D images into the air from a smartphone-sized device and interact with them without touch. Marketon plans to showcase this new product at CES 2026 in Las Vegas this January, aiming to capture the global fandom market.

The ‘Mobile Hologram’ leverages Marketon’s proven mid-air projection technology—applied initially in education and exhibitions—and optimizes it for K-pop artist content. Fans can enjoy immersive performances, interviews, and fan meetups with the naked eye—no monitor or VR gear needed. With an integrated AI agent, users can use voice commands or gestures to play, pause, zoom, or rotate content. Personalized playlists and recommendations based on fan preferences are also available.

Marketon’s hologram technology has already been successfully deployed in venues such as the Seodaemun Museum of Natural History, multiple schools in Korea, financial institutions in Singapore, and major banks, demonstrating high engagement and immersion. It performs well even in bright lighting, requires no reflective surfaces, and has fewer installation constraints. It is also more hygienic than VR gear, while being safer and more precise than propeller-type holograms. The new product brings this technology into the K-culture and entertainment space.

body.cap: Marketon’s 24-inch holographic display showing a floating dinosaur in mid-air. Users can zoom and rotate the image using touch-free finger gestures | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Marketon defines its latest product as a “concert in your hand.” Unlike larger 24-inch units, this portable version is designed with mobility and battery life in mind. It is ideal for use in concerts, fan signings, merchandise shops, and pop-up stores. Without the need for a monitor or VR goggles, the device provides immersive experiences that make fans feel like they are in the same space as their favorite artists.

“Our goal was not just to create a new type of display, but a new kind of experience,” said CEO Chang Joon Yang. “We wanted to deliver a sense of presence between fans and artists, wherever they are in the world. That’s why we focused on enhancing portability and real-time interaction.”

He added, “The Mobile Hologram will become an essential tool in global K-pop tours, transforming how fans engage with performances. Its AI agent integration enables personalized content delivery, making it fundamentally different from existing hologram devices.”

At CES 2026, Marketon will focus on the ‘AI & Entertainment’ track, aiming to build global partnerships with K-pop agencies, global fan platforms, and merchandise distributors. It is also preparing artist-specific AI agents to enable fan communication services. With high K-pop demand in markets such as North America, Europe, and Japan, the company expects to finalize major global contracts during the exhibition.
